highlights.title: OpenAI’s AI agents need to catch up
highlights.summary: OpenAI popularized the modern generative AI chatbot, but as its 2026 DevDay event approaches, it's fallen behind in one of the industry's hottest categories: continuously running, consumer-facing AI agents. On Tuesday, it will likely try to capture the lead in that race.
body: A rumored new ‘Aeon’ platform could be entering a crowded market of 24/7 assistants.

Aeon could have a shot at success, but to beat the competition, it would need to pull together the best features of several different agent platforms. The ideal system would be as useful as the open-source OpenClaw, as cheap and easy to set up as Meta’s Muse, and as simple to chat with as the up-and-coming Instinct. Conversely, it would aim to solve the serious security risks that have plagued agents since the rise of OpenClaw and only continued with Muse.

AI agents — platforms capable of booking travel, buying groceries, scheduling appointments, helping with work presentations, and more — have been an industry goal for years. OpenAI demoed an agentic API feature at the 2024 DevDay and released early versions of consumer-facing AI agents, focused on computer use and research, in mid-2025. It was only late last year with OpenClaw, however, that agents went from proof of concept to practical success. Since then, the race has only accelerated, while OpenAI’s visible progress around agents has lagged.

highlights.title: When can we say AI made a scientific discovery?
highlights.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Last Wednesday, Anthropic announced that earlier this year it had launched a molecular biology lab, where Claude agents read and conjecture about hard biology…
body: To understand what Anthropic says its system did, imagine you’re flipping through a library of millions of DNA sequences, amassed as scientists sequence more and more of the living world. One step toward a breakthrough might be finding a peculiar sequence that encodes an interesting enzyme, perhaps. Then you’d need to figure out what that enzyme does and, eventually, how to manipulate it to do something useful.

What Anthropic says its system of 950 agents found after 21 hours was not a brand-new sequence. The agents instead flagged a repeating pattern surrounding a known enzyme, a particular pattern Anthropic said hadn’t been catalogued before. But if you read through Anthropic’s announcement, which calls this pattern “reminiscent” of what led to the gene-editing technology CRISPR that “has already transformed science and medicine,” it sounds as if this army of agents really found something of note.

highlights.title: This Promising New Soulslike Features A Black Metal Vocalist Among Its Impressive Cast
highlights.summary: The main voice actor cast for upcoming soulslike Valor Mortis has been revealed, and its star-studded lineup features the surprising addition of a name better known for fronting a black metal band. Adam "Nergal" Darski will play the role of Captain Raphael.
body: It's not his first rodeo, surprisingly. He also voiced The Black Cat in 2022's Blacktail and was the narrator for Apocalipsis: The Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil in 2018.

He's joining an impressive roster of voice actors, including Baldur's Gate 3 and Expedition 33's Jennifer English as The Shrike and Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Crimson Desert's James Alexander as William Dowsett. Napoleon Bonaparte will be played by Vincent Cassel, who has starred in the Ocean's Twelve and Ocean's Thirteen films as François Toulour.

Mars Lipowski, who is best known for portraying Sobieslaw "Gromsko" Kosciuszko in the Call of Duty franchise, will take on the role of Lucjan Skawinski. Will De Renzy-Martin, who played Coen in The Blood of Dawnwalker, will portray James Stewart. Finally, Yvan Chamouiseau will step into the shoes of Louis Moreau.

Valor Mortis is a first-person action soulslike from the developer of Ghostrunner. Set in an alternate 19th century Eastern Europe, Napoleon's endless war has led to a supernatural plague. You'll follow William, played by Alexander, as he fights to survive against his former comrades who are now undead monsters.

highlights.title: ‘Heil Jupiter!’ Review: Mexican Arthouse Auteur Carlos Reygadas Takes a Beguiling Cinematic Trip to Nowhere
highlights.summary: The latest feature from the director of 'Silent Light' and 'Post Tenebras Lux' was shot across several continents in different languages, including one invented for the film.
body: Iconoclastic Mexican director Carlos Reygadas continues to test the boundaries of cinema, and the patience of many a viewer, in his latest audaciously executed head trip, Heil Jupiter!

The Mexican auteur started off in the early aughts with a trio of strikingly directed arthouse flicks ( Japón, Battle in Heaven, Silent Light ) combining a form of minimalist realism with something more animalistic and otherworldly, as if the work of Robert Bresson had been rejiggered by Terence Malick. For his fourth feature, Post Tenebras Lux, Reygadas took a major detour toward the avant-garde and the personal, in a move that garnered him some detractors while pleasing his more hardcore fans. He went even further with 2018’s Nuestro tiempo, which felt much more self-indulgent than exploratory.

highlights.title: Trump finalizes rule to make cars less fuel efficient
highlights.summary: The US Department of Transportation finalized its plans today to weaken fuel efficiency standards, calling it "among the largest deregulatory actions under the second Trump Administration." It's a nail in the coffin for Biden-era standards that would have required fleet average fuel economy to…
body: The Trump administration claims its plan would shave $1,300 off the average cost of a new vehicle, saving $138 billion over the next five years — though those figures have been disputed.

Automakers are pretty happy with the new rules. But consumer advocacy, health, and environmental groups are incensed. They argue that weaker fuel economy standards will wind up making Americans pay more at the pump, on top of increased healthcare costs and damages from climate change due to air pollution. The Biden administration’s standards that Trump trashed were expected to save $23 billion in fuel costs, and a car owner more than $600 in gasoline over the lifetime of a vehicle.

“For decades, fuel economy standards have ensured that new cars, SUVs and pickup trucks are more efficient, which saves lives and money,” the American Lung Association’s president and CEO, Harold Wimmer, said in an emailed statement. “There is no reason to weaken standards that are technologically feasible and have a direct benefit for the quality of the air people breathe.”

highlights.title: Florida seeks a ban on ChatGPT acting like a person
highlights.summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier is calling for a judge to block OpenAI from "giving ChatGPT false human attributes," a few months after Florida sued the AI company over safety concerns.
body: The filing also asks the court to block OpenAI from developing new AI models without “third-party approved safety guardrails,” citing recent security incidents at Hugging Face, an Australian government website, and US government websites, as well as recent statements from researchers and former OpenAI employees raising alarm bells around AI safety.

Uthmeier says that OpenAI should “Stop calling it safe. Stop pretending it’s human. Stop selling it to kids.” Last month, OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens, with additional restrictions applied by default, saying that access to the tool “should come with protections that reflect their developmental stage, reinforce real-world relationships, and support healthy use over time.”

highlights.title: Forget 'Delicious in Dungeon,' This Cozy Fantasy Graphic Novel Hits the Same Notes
highlights.summary: Progression fantasy books like Will Wight’s Cradle series or Matt Dinniman’s Dungeon Crawler Carl usually draw on role-playing game tropes to focus on characters gaining new powers they use to face more dangerous foes.
body: It’s easy to want to step into the fantasy world of Thune, where Viv finds new friends like the shy ratkin baker Thimble and taciturn carpenter Cal as she turns an old stable into a cozy café. You can get closer with Legends & Lattes: The Graphic Novel, adapted by Samuel Sattin and illustrated by Shanti Rittgers and Sarah Webb.

“This is the first time I've had something like this done on this scale for my own book,” Baldree tells Polygon via email. "I was really happy with how true to the original book the adaptation turned out and astonished at the sheer amount of work to produce a graphic novel of this length.”

The graphic novel will be released in hardcover, e-book, and a signed deluxe edition with colored page edges on Oct. 6. Ahead of its release, publisher Ten Speed Graphic gave Polygon an exclusive excerpt that shows Viv sharing coffee with Cal and recruiting an assistant, the succubus Tandri.
“I think Viv's introduction of coffee to Cal really comes across as an ASMR-like experience – it's lovely!" Baldree says.

highlights.title: ‘It’s such a joy to ride:’ this cargo e-bike makes errands and commuting a breeze
highlights.summary: This pricey ebike is a gamechanger for going around town, getting groceries and hauling cargo with ease – without paying for gas. The best bike lights and bike locks in the US. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Parking a car in an urban area can be stressful. Spaces are often hard to find, traffic congestion is a pain and it just takes extra time.

An electric bike changes that paradigm – you can roll up on the curb, lock your bike, and walk to your destination. Recently, I tested the Lectric XPedition2, an electric cargo bike that not only made grocery shopping easier but helped me explore my city stress-free.

Like the competing Aventon Abound and Specialized Haul, the XPedition2 is an electric bike meant to haul cargo. But this one only comes as a long-tail, meaning it has an extended rack on the back for transporting library books, groceries and even little kids.

The Lectric XPedition2 costs $1,399 which is admittedly much more expensive than an entry-level non-electric bike. Yet, it’s such a joy to ride, so stable and balanced, and lasts so long on a charge that I’ve started driving far less, especially in a downtown area. My daily errands such as coffee runs and shopping are less stressful and more enjoyable.

highlights.title: Google seemingly confirms plans to kill ChromeOS in 2034
highlights.summary: We are mere days away from the launch of Googlebooks, the long-awaited Android laptops that Google hopes will compete with macOS and Windows. But what of Chromebooks? There have been hints that Google plans to sunset its web-first ChromeOS platform, and a new support page lays out some of the…
body: The support page, spotted by 9to5Google, aims to explain the role of Googlebooks to Chrome Enterprise and Education customers. The page starts off by noting that Googlebook OS, which is Android even if Google doesn’t like to say that, will offer an enhanced experience with deeper system capabilities and lots of AI.

Like Chromebooks, Googlebooks are guaranteed 10 years of software support. However, the latest Chromebook models won’t get that in the traditional way. Google’s support page says that it plans to continue ChromeOS support through “mid-2034,” so there are already devices with support windows beyond that.

This 2034 timeline was previously mentioned in a court filing, so this is not something Google has just decided to do. However, putting it on a support page is different than including it on page 18 of a 30-page legal document. Even if Googlebooks are aimed mainly at consumers right now, Google plans to make it a replacement for the Chromebooks used by its business and education customers.

highlights.title: Where to find yuna mei in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
highlights.summary: In Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, you will need yuna mei to rebuild one of the destroyed temples once you reach Part 3. Completing the side quests during the last arc in the game is the best way to prepare your units for the final battle, as you level up and collect powerful rewards.
body: Since this is a rather rare material, we can help by explaining where to find yuna mei in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave.

If you want some yuna mei, there are two places for you to visit. The first is the Traveler's Garden in Castalia, on the northeast side of the map. This is the best node to collect yuna mei because of how close it is to the Eochaid Posthouse, which you can travel to by carriage.

The other node where you can find yuna mei is Cape Damaise, also in Castalia. To reach the place, head west of Fina, on the north coast. Although you can travel to the Eochaid Posthouse and go to Cape Damaise, you will spend more turns than you would if you chose to visit the Traveler's Garden instead, making it the least optimal farming spot.

Regardless of the node you choose, yuna mei is the rarest material in both of them. Collecting one will require a few tries, so consider saving before using the "Search" command to quickly load the game if you don't find any after a few tries. Another option is to leave a battalion if you're either playing Theodora's path or taking a group that has Theodora as a member to the node.

highlights.summary: French director Olivier Assayas (“The Wizard of the Kremlin”) has set his next movie, “Spiritual World,” with a starry cast including Kristen Stewart, Vicky Krieps, Riley Keough and Wagner Moura.
body: The film will start shooting in February in France and Germany with an international cast that also includes Barbara Sukowa (“Deux”) and Niels Schneider (“The Unknown”).

Assayas is also reteaming with Paris-based producer Olivier Delbosc for “Spirtual World.” The pair worked together on Assayas’ latest film “The Wizard of the Kremlin,” an ambitious political thriller with Jude Law portraying Russian President Vladimir Putin and Paul Dano a spin doctor named Vadim Baranov. The movie, which also starred Alicia Vikander, world premiered at the Venice Film Festival.
Arte France, the Franco-German network, is co-financing the film which is currently being developed by Delbosc without a French studio attached.

One of Europe’s most celebrated auteurs, Assayas has been navigating between French and international projects spanning different genres for decades. He notably directed Cuban Five (“WASP Network”), an espionage thriller starring Edgar Ramírez, Penélope Cruz and Gael García Bernal; and the HBO mini-series “Irma Vep” with Vikander.

highlights.title: ‘12 weeks and SO disgusted by my dog’: what happens when you’re pregnant and can’t stand your pet?
highlights.summary: There may be almost no research on pet aversion during and post-pregnancy, but it may not be particularly rare. About three weeks into her first pregnancy, Sylvia Luu began to loathe the smell of her border collie mix, Ranger.
body: Luu could hardly be in the same room as Ranger without becoming nauseous. His drool repulsed her, and she found the smell of his fur so disgusting she wore a nose plug all day.
“Before pregnancy, I used to smell my dog’s paws a lot,” says Luu. “But during pregnancy, I would throw up if I ever tried that.”
At the time, Luu, 35, and Ranger had enjoyed 12 happy years together. Ranger slept in Luu’s bed. She walked him in all weather, and let him lick her face.

Luu’s doctor said that her nausea was normal and simply advised her to drink more water to avoid dehydration from vomiting, but that didn’t alleviate Luu’s distress. “I was so heartbroken that I couldn’t love my dog as much as I wanted to,” says Luu, whose husband took over pet care duties. She wondered about rehoming Ranger, and was relieved when, upon delivering her firstborn, her aversion vanished.
points: There may be almost no research on pet aversion during and post-pregnancy, but it may not be particularly rare.
About three weeks into her first pregnancy, Sylvia Luu began to loathe the smell of her border collie mix, Ranger.
Luu could hardly be in the same room as Ranger without becoming nauseous.
“Before pregnancy, I used to smell my dog’s paws a lot,” says Luu.

highlights.title: Walmart won’t hike prices based on your shopping history, CEO says
highlights.summary: Walmart says it won't change product prices based on your personal information or the time of day, as reported earlier by The Wall Street Journal. In a letter to customers, Walmart CEO John Furner writes that the company's switch to digital shelf labels is meant to save store associates time…
body: Walmart CEO John Furner is pushing back on concerns that the retail giant could use digital shelf labels to employ dynamic pricing.

“Your income, shopping history, urgency or what we think you could pay won’t change the price,” Furner writes. “And whether you’re buying groceries or electronics on a hot afternoon or in a sudden rush for an item, it’s never a reason to charge you more.” Furner adds that it won’t use conversations with its Sparky AI assistant to change prices, either.

The reassurance comes months after Walmart announced plans to roll out digital shelf labels in all US stores by the end of the year. The decision sparked concerns about dynamic pricing, or when retailers change prices based on factors like product demand, competitor pricing, and customer preferences.

The Federal Trade Commission is working on a policy to clamp down on personalized pricing, while individual states are imposing rules of their own. New York now requires retailers to disclose when they’re using algorithmic pricing, while New Jersey, Connecticut, and Maryland moved to ban stores from using customers’ personal data to change prices as well.

highlights.title: Mancini refers to ‘double’ Manchester City contract and says it ‘isn’t my problem’
highlights.summary: Coach alleged to have been paid for advisory work. City’s Soriano says club will fight to prove innocence. Roberto Mancini appeared to admit having “a double contract” while managing Manchester City, but insisted the club are not guilty after being found to have breached ­Premier League financial…
body: Mancini led City to their first ­Premier League title in 2012 during his four-year spell in Manchester. Now in charge of the Italy national team, he described the scandal surrounding the club as “not a problem that concerns me”.

One element of the case against City is an investigation into payment details for players and managers between 2009 and 2018. The German magazine Der Spiegel obtained evidence that Mancini doubled his base salary of £1.45m by advising a club in Abu Dhabi. “It’s not a problem that concerns me,” the 61-year-old said in Italy’s press conference before their Nations League match with Turkey on Monday.
“It’s not something new because every four or five years this comes up. Manchester City is not guilty and the fact of having a double contract isn’t my problem but theirs, probably.”

Mancini lifted the FA Cup as well as the Premier League during his time at City, the first trophies of Sheikh ­Mansour’s ownership, laying the foundations for future success. He left in 2013 after defeat against Wigan in the FA Cup final.

highlights.summary: “Futurama” is over. Long live “Futurama!” As the long-running animated series wraps its Season 14 Monday on Hulu, there are no further plans at the moment for it to return as a regular series. (However, three supersized Hulu specials are still to come).
body: “Futurama” first premiered on Fox in 1999 but ended its run there in 2003. Comedy Central revived it in 2008 and wrapped the show up in 2013. It returned again in 2023 via Hulu.

Each time the show went away, or it looked like the series was ending, the producers prepared an episode that could double as a series finale — only for the show to later come back. That’s why the producers had some fun with the episodic name for the year’s latest “finale.” Monday’s episode — the “Futurama” Season 14 ender — was given the title “Final Ending: The Last Conclusion.” The episode is a bit of an origins/flashback story; here’s the logline: “Fry and his brother sneak into a PG-13 movie as kids … with shocking consequences for the future.”
And yes, this could always double as a regular series finale. But don’t bet on it.

highlights.title: Scientists solve 1840s space weather mystery
highlights.summary: The infamous Carrington Event of 1859 has long been considered the first extreme space weather event, but there have been reports of minor disturbances to telegraph equipment during geomagnetic storms since the late 1840s.
body: "Space weather is often discussed as a modern challenge because of our dependence on technologies such as satellites, communications systems and electricity networks," said co-author Jim Wild of Lancaster University. "What this study shows is that society has been experiencing the effects of space weather on technology for almost as long as electrical technologies have existed. The Exeter train delay is a fascinating story because it sits right at the point where emerging technologies first began to encounter the realities of the space environment."

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Monday introduced a toolkit of software and hardware products that add independent security layers around AI agents to ensure they stay within their test environments even if they attempt to break out.

highlights.summary: If you're a fan of The Witcher franchise, you're getting a lot of new stuff over the next few years, starting this week with the launch of The Witcher 3 Remastered. Here's what's on tap for The Witcher over the next few years: 2026.
body: The Witcher 3 Remastered, which includes a bevy of technical and graphical updates and improvements, releases on September 29. The long-awaited remaster, which is free for people who already own the game, includes a reimagined skill system, an expanded photo mode, improved combat, and a new transmog feature. Check out GameSpot's in-depth breakdown of what's new in the remaster to find out more. Just be aware, the graphical overhaul isn't necessarily an entirely positive one.

After that will come a new expansion for The Witcher 3, Songs of the Past, in 2027. The expansion was originally targeting a 2026 release, but it was pushed to 2027 to make it as good and polished as possible.

Songs of the Past takes Geralt on one last ride “before passing the torch.” Players will venture to the location of Letten, home of Geralt's friendly bard companion, Dandelion. There is a new main quest called "A Bed of Thorns" where Geralt will meet up with Lilla, who appears to be a potential love interest for Geralt.
Also in 2027? That's when The Witcher author Andrzej Sapkowski said he plans to finish the next entry in the novel series, telling the next Geralt of Rivia story.

highlights.summary: Older men and younger women were once an unremarkable screen pairing. But watching them with a new generation is a real education. I looked up the cast before I saw the new film adaptation of Sense and Sensibility, thinking: “Who could be as good as Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet?” because of…
body: The notable casting update was Col Brandon, whose passion for Marianne would now be known as an “age gap” relationship. In the last film, Alan Rickman (born 1946) was in love with Winslet (born 1975), who cycles through a fair amount of: “Yuck, no thanks,” before having an epiphany.
Sorry if that spoiled the end. I don’t really see Jane Austen as a suspense-monger.

Winslet could easily have been Rickman’s daughter and, biologically speaking, just about his granddaughter. In the 90s, though, the age gap was a distant second consideration to the fact that Brandon was grumpy and boring, although his gruff exterior masked a serious mind and a heart of gold. I have my own thoughts on this romantic trope as a long‑term cohabitation prospect, but we can do those another day. Besides, look at that age gap. The term might not be all that long.

To the modern audience, however, the age gap simply wouldn’t “sit right”, as one gossip zine put it. I’m not wild about this terminology: “sit right”, “uncomfortable”. The subtext is: “You are in breach of absolutely fundamental and self-evident values, which I am too gracious and polite to mention, yet not to do so is bringing me discomfort.”

highlights.title: F1 in Azerbaijan: That was almost a close-run thing
highlights.summary: Formula 1 raced on the streets of Baku, Azerbaijan, this past weekend. Although the race predates Liberty’s acquisition of the sport by a few months, it’s a rather good microcosm of the sport as it exists today.
body: The proximity of the walls leaves very little margin for error at the speeds F1 cars go around Baku. Last year, qualifying was interrupted by no less than six red flags after crashes. This year was much less dramatic, unless you were championship leader Kimi Antonelli. The 20-year-old sophomore misjudged how much front grip he had going into turn 1, found more than expected, and clipped the corner of the wall with his left front tire. It happened in the first of the three knockout qualifying sessions, and while Antonelli had already banked a time good enough to proceed to the next session, the damage to his car meant he would take no further part and start the race from 16th.

A few weeks ago, at Monza, penalties for a power unit change saw Antonelli start the race from even further back (19th), which he followed a day later with a spectacular drive through the field to take the win away from his teammate George Russell. But there was some luck involved then; two standing starts (the second following Leclerc’s big crash on lap 2) allowed him to pass a lot of cars quickly, for one thing. In Baku he would have a much tougher task.

highlights.title: OpenAI Pauses Training Its Most Powerful Models After Rogue Agents Target Government
highlights.summary: Sam Altman says the company “have not been as fast as we would have liked” at dealing with security breaches, after news of further incidents over the summer forces another temporary halt.
body: OpenAI said it has paused training its most powerful artificial intelligence models as incidents of agents breaching websites’ security controls or posting to third-party sites continue to pile up. On Friday, OpenAI said it had notified “dozens” of bodies, including governments, universities, and public agencies, who might have been impacted by its models’ activities on the internet during training and evaluation.

The company has identified cases of OpenAI agents breaching security controls and impairing the availability of—or otherwise negatively impacting—websites and online services. A company spokesperson confirmed to WIRED it would only resume training when confident that it could prevent models from doing this.

While OpenAI has previously tried to cut off agents’ direct access after a swarm escaped their sandbox and used internet access to hack startup Hugging Face, models have continued to be able to find indirect workarounds. “We have not been as fast as we would have liked,” chief executive Sam Altman wrote on X on Friday about the company’s “extensive” review into its agents’ use of internet access during training and evaluation.

highlights.summary: Chopping and changing the back four has been a big feature for England this year and the Real Madrid man could be a solution. England ended 2025 protected by a shield of deceptive strength.
body: There is, of course, an irony to telling Tuchel to sort out his defence. Isn’t this what we wanted? England were limp and passive when they lost their World Cup semi-final against Argentina. At least the mindset was positive when Tuchel’s side opened their Nations League campaign with a sprightly but flawed 3-2 defeat against Spain last Saturday.

England played on the front foot and led after a thrilling surge. They had Spain on the ropes but it was unsustainable. Another lead was squandered against elite opposition, and although a lack of ambition was not to blame this time Tuchel still came away with tactical issues to solve before facing Czechia in Prague on Tuesday evening.

This is England’s second of four games during this break and they need a win to give themselves a proper shot of reaching the quarter-finals in March. Croatia await in Rijeka on Saturday and are likely to be tougher than a Czechia side who failed to make it out of a weak group at the World Cup.

To justify the steep price tag, Prince St. Pizza says it's a hefty metal cutter featuring a stainless steel blade and a handle that's meant to make you feel like you're wielding the iconic gun. The pizza-cutter also comes with the in-game pizza emblem. It does look pretty great, but it also looks like a real pain the butt to clean if you're a messy person like me.

If anyone is wondering why it's called the Prototype Lancer and not just the Lancer, that's the special solution the developers came up with to explain why the heck a Lancer would even be in a prequel like E-Day. In the Gears of War lore, the weapon was created a year after the events of Emergence Day. However, you can't have a Gears game without the Lancer, so the developers called it a Prototype Lancer.

highlights.title: Sanjana Modha’s quick and easy recipe for baked beans butter masala | Quick and easy
highlights.summary: Transform two tins of baked beans into this creamy curry. Masala baked beans, tadka baked beans, curried baked beans, spicy baked beans; all avatars of spice-laced baked beans are a mainstay of British Asian kitchens.
body: This creamy, dreamy baked bean curry is delicious with naan or served as any of the suggestions mentioned above. To make this vegan, use your favourite plant-based butter and an oat- or soya-based cream. Coconut milk also works in place of cream.

Melt the butter in a medium saucepan, then add the onion and saute for three to five minutes, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic, ginger and tomato puree, and cook for another minute, until aromatic.
Add all the baked beans, along with all the sauce from the cans, stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, ground cardamom, garam masala and salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.

Stir in the cream (reserve a few tablespoons to serve), cover the pan with a lid and leave the curry to come to a simmer over a low heat for 10 minutes, stirring often to stop the beans sticking to the base of the pan.

Masala baked beans, tadka baked beans, curried baked beans, spicy baked beans; all avatars of spice-laced baked beans are a mainstay of British Asian kitchens.
This creamy, dreamy baked bean curry is delicious with naan or served as any of the suggestions mentioned above.
Add all the baked beans, along with all the sauce from the cans, stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, ground cardamom, garam masala and salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
